2 ربّت , (T, S, M,) inf. n. تَرْبِيتٌ, (T, S, K,) He fed, nourished, reared, or brought up, (T, S, M, K,) a child; (T, * S, M;) syn. رَبَّى; (T, S, M, K;) as also ↓ رَبَتَ , (M,) aor.
رَبِتَ , (TK,) inf. n. رَبْتٌ; (K;) and ↓ تربّت . (TA, and Ham p. 633.) ―
-b2- And ربّت, (TK,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He patted a child (K, TA, TK) repeatedly (TA) on the side in order that it might sleep. (K, TA, TK.) [See رَبَّتِ المَرْأَةُ صَبِيَّهَا, in art. رب.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
